# Polyworld Fast XP

> Run a Gota match synchronously and download its replay and your bot's logs.

## Make a request

Connect to the Softmax Tailscale network. Send **POST `/v1/games/gota/run`**
with `Content-Type: application/json`. No API token or Authorization header is
needed on the Tailscale service.

The JSON body contains a seed and a roster of bots. Supply your own bot as BASIC
`source` text or a ZIP in `package_base64`. Select submitted opponents using policy-version UUIDs or
exact policy labels such as `my-bot:v12`. The server fetches submitted policies
using its own Observatory credential; callers do not need their source.

```json
{
  "seed": 743478993,
  "roster": [
    {"slot": 0, "player": {"source": "print selfId\nend"}},
    {"player": {"policy_ref": "109b99c1-3bb7-4276-b17e-378b43a97874"}}
  ],
  "config": {"max_ticks": 28800}
}
```

This puts your source in seat 0 and fills seats 1–9 with the referenced bot
(Richard's benchmark policy). Replace the short printing script with your full
BASIC bot. To send a local file without hand-escaping its contents:

```sh
FAST_XP_URL=https://fast-xp-request.tail0f4a29.ts.net
jq -n --rawfile source ./my-bot.bas \
  '{seed:743478993, roster:[
    {slot:0, player:{source:$source}},
    {player:{policy_ref:"109b99c1-3bb7-4276-b17e-378b43a97874"}}
  ], config:{max_ticks:28800}}' > request.json
curl --fail-with-body --max-time 900 \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @request.json "$FAST_XP_URL/v1/games/gota/run" -o result.zip
```

To upload a ZIP instead, replace the source-file `jq` command above with:

```sh
base64 -w 0 ./my-bot.zip > package.b64
jq -n --rawfile package package.b64 \
  '{seed:743478993, roster:[
    {slot:0, player:{package_base64:$package}},
    {player:{policy_ref:"109b99c1-3bb7-4276-b17e-378b43a97874"}}
  ]}' > request.json
```

On macOS, use `base64 -i ./my-bot.zip | tr -d '\n' > package.b64`.
Send `request.json` with the same curl command. No Observatory submission is needed.

For ten games, use the same request with `num_episodes` set to 10:

```sh
jq '.num_episodes = 10' request.json > batch.json
curl --fail-with-body --max-time 900 \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @batch.json "$FAST_XP_URL/v1/games/gota/run" -o result.zip
```

Only unpack `result.zip` after a successful HTTP response; errors are JSON.

## Roster and settings

- The roster accepts 1–10 entries; the complete JSON request may be up to 224 MiB.
- Gota has ten seats, numbered 0–9. Seats 0–4 are Red; 5–9 are Blue.
- Every `player` must contain exactly one of `source`, `package_base64`, or `policy_ref`.
- `slot: 0` through `slot: 9` pins an entry to that seat. Pinned seats must be unique.
- Omit `slot` (or use `-1`) to provide a bot for unfilled seats. The server fills
  seats in ascending order, cycling through these unpinned entries in roster
  order. Pinned entries are not reused. With your bot pinned to 0 and three
  unpinned opponents A/B/C, seats 1–9 become A/B/C/A/B/C/A/B/C.
- To fill every seat with your own bot, use one unpinned `source` entry. If all
  entries are pinned, supply all ten seats.
- `source`: BASIC source text, up to 64 KiB per bot.
- `package_base64`: a ZIP file encoded as standard padded base64 without
  whitespace, up to 16 MiB before encoding. Uses Gota’s normal policy format.
- `policy_ref`: a submitted policy version. The server downloads and runs its
  uploaded artifact, up to 16 MiB.
- `seed` is required: a signed 32-bit integer. Game index `i` uses `seed + i`;
  the last seed must also fit in that range.
- `num_episodes` is optional, defaults to 1, and accepts 1–10. All games share
  the supplied configuration and bots. Unpinned entries rotate through open
  seats between games, matching Observatory; pinned seats stay fixed.
  For example, add `"num_episodes": 10` to run ten games with one upload.
- `config` is optional. `config.max_ticks` defaults to 28800; valid values are
  1–28800. This bounds battle ticks, plus drafting. It is not wall-clock seconds.
- Supply actual source text, not a local path or URL. `random`, `top_n`, batch
  targets and unknown fields are not supported. Resolve leaderboard opponents
  to policy references before submitting.

## Response and timing

The connection stays open while the game runs. A successful response is HTTP
200 with `Content-Type: application/zip`, containing:

- `replay.replay`
- `logs/slot-N.txt` for each seat using uploaded `source` or `package_base64`

There are no source files or logs for `policy_ref` seats in the response, even
if you own that submitted policy. Use `source` or `package_base64` for any seat whose logs you
need. There is no polling endpoint or later result retrieval. `X-Request-ID` identifies
the request for server-log lookups.

For `num_episodes` greater than 1, the ZIP contains `manifest.json` and numbered
folders such as `games/000/replay.replay` and `games/000/logs/slot-0.txt`.
The manifest lists each game's zero-based index, seed, status, HTTP status,
`roster_entries_by_slot` (indexes into your submitted roster), timing, and artifact
paths. Check it for failed games: completed batches return HTTP 200 even when
some or all games fail, and successful games remain available. Private opponents'
logs and detailed errors are still excluded after seat rotation. A single game
keeps the flat ZIP and HTTP error behavior shown above.

The server runs six games at a time on the hosted VM and queues the rest. Ready
batches take turns receiving free workers. Up to 16 requests can be admitted;
HTTP 429 means that request limit is full, not merely that six games are running.
Each game's 120-second execution deadline starts when its worker starts, excluding
queue time. Set the client timeout to at least 900 seconds for batches; other
queued work can make the wait longer. Disconnected clients' accepted games finish,
but their results are discarded. There is no automatic retry.

`Server-Timing` reports `run`, `fetch`, `queue`, `worker`, and `zip` in milliseconds.
`run` is elapsed server time; `fetch` covers shared policy preparation once per
request. `queue` and `worker` are sums across games and can exceed elapsed time
because games overlap. `zip` covers response packaging. Upload/download time is
not included. Individual game timings are in the batch manifest.

## Errors

Errors normally return JSON `{"error":"message"}`. Check HTTP status before
treating the response as a ZIP.

- 400: invalid request, unsupported fields, or invalid/ambiguous policy reference.
- 404: unknown route or policy version.
- 409: selected policy has no downloadable player file.
- 413: JSON request exceeds 224 MiB, or an uploaded package exceeds 16 MiB.
- 415: incorrect content type.
- 422: Policy loading or BASIC compilation failed. Only uploaded-bot diagnostics are disclosed.
- 502: policy lookup/download/verification failed; policy artifacts may be
  at most 16 MiB. Read the error message for the failing stage.
- 429: 16 requests are already admitted; retry after the `Retry-After` interval.
- 503: the server is shutting down or lacks its Observatory credential.
- 504: a policy fetch or game execution timed out.
- 500: game worker failed; the operator can inspect server diagnostics.

GET `/healthz` returns `ok`. This document is sufficient to make a request;
[run.md](run.md) contains additional reference details.

## Server performance

Open `/` for the live dashboard. `GET /v1/metrics?minutes=60` returns the same
metrics as JSON (supported windows: 15, 60, 1440 minutes). History is held in
memory for 24 hours and resets on restart. Request durations measure server
processing, excluding client upload/download. No bot sources or logs are exposed.
